Subject: CuraNova: international transfer scoping + evidence ask

Hi Rafael —

Thanks for the demo last week. Our legal team is starting the DPA review and we need a short mapping of how Redwood routes EU/UK customer data for CuraNova workloads. Specifically:

- Which transfer mechanism you expect us to rely on (EU SCCs, UK IDTA / UK addendum, or DTIA/TIA pattern) for accounts that use both London and Dublin regions.
- A current subprocessor list and attestation for any third parties that may see content or logs (including any caching/edge providers).
- A short evidence pack we can hand to our privacy counsel (logs retention, export controls, host locations by service).

Our deadline to present to legal is 10 May; is it possible to get an index of documents by then?

Appreciate a quick plan and any immediate blockers.

Thanks,
Claire
Claire Dent | Head of Legal Ops | CuraNova

Claire — thanks for the clear list. Quick plan below and we can follow with a 30m call if helpful.

Plan / immediate deliverables (targeting 5/9):
1) Evidence index (spreadsheet) that maps each ask to a document we can share. See attached: curanova-redwood-evidence-index.xlsx.
2) Subprocessor catalog (CSV) + attestation PDF: redwood-subprocessor-catalog.csv and subprocessor-attestation-20280503.pdf (attached).
3) Recommended transfer approach: default = EU SCCs for cross-border processing + optional UK Addendum (IDTA) if you require UK-residency guarantees for affected data sets. We will include a short note showing how the SCCs map to our routing policies (regions: eu-west-1 / eu-west-2).
4) TIA/DTIA scoping: Jonas will provide a short technical addendum describing transient processing nodes (prefix caching, onshore fallback) and where KV caches may be stored.
5) DPA redlines: we can produce a DocuSign-ready packet for signature once redlines are agreed. Link: https://docusign.example.com/ENVELOPE12345

If these deliverables match what your counsel needs, we’ll prioritize the evidence index and subprocessor attestation first.

Next steps:
- Laura: drive a single package for legal (index + attestation + high-level routing note).
- Jonas: produce the TIA sketch and note on caching/transit nodes by EOD 5/5.
- Kimberly: confirm any conditional processing / on-prem options and provide retention policy extract.

If you prefer a quick handoff call, I can book 30 minutes tomorrow afternoon.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Account Lead | Redwood Inference

Claire / team — adding a few specifics from the controls side so your counsel has concrete entries to review: 

- Subprocessors (short list): AWS (eu-west-1, eu-west-2 compute & storage), FastEdge CDN (edge caching only, no persistent storage), LogStore Co (aggregated logs; pseudonymized), KMS provider (HSM-backed key management). Full CSV attached.
- Retention: request logs retention extract (we keep request logs for 90 days by default; customer-configurable longer retention on Dedicated/Private).
- Caching & onshore fallback: our prefix caching can keep tokenized KV entries in-region; for firms requiring UK-only residency we recommend Private or Dedicated with explicit region pinning — otherwise SCCs + UK Addendum are typical.
- Attestation: we can provide a signed subprocessor attestation (attached). For any high-assurance customers we offer an optional on-prem package (air-gapped) — would require procurement + longer lead time.

On the DTIAs/TIAs: we maintain a sampling plan for transient nodes — Jonas, can you confirm expected TTL for KV caches in EU/UK scenarios?

-Kim
Kimberly Park | Head, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
